column1: # One owner for the fleet unit list.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The same list of units was hand-maintained in six places
# bin/praetorium-status.sh, bin/local_tier_eval.sh) and the six disagreed in six ways.
# The best of them covered 9 standing units; eight units appeared in NONE of them, so
# invisible to every report on the box. This file replaces those six lists. It must not
# become a seventh: a consumer that needs a different subset FILTERS this file, and a
# consumer that needs a unit not declared in design/agents/*.toml is telling you the
# manifest is wrong, not that it needs its own list.
# WHY IT IS A COMMITTED LITERAL AND NOT GENERATED AT RUN TIME. bin/deploy ships
# `bin profiles docs CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md README.md config systemd` — `design/` is NOT
# among them and ~/agent-workforce/design does not exist. Anything reading the manifests
# at run time works in the repo and silently empties in the tree systemd actually execs.
# So the manifests stay the source, this file is their materialised projection, and
# tests/test_fleet_ownership.sh asserts the two are equal. That is open-decisions.md D4's
# answer (b) — literals kept, asserted against the manifest — applied to a second list.
# HOW TO CHANGE IT. Edit design/agents/<persona>.toml first, then re-materialise here.
# The test fails in both directions, so neither half can drift alone.
# SCOPE IS LOAD-BEARING. `user` units are invisible to system-scope systemctl. A consumer
# that ignores this column reports a live user timer as missing. Until 2026-09-02 scope was
# stated in prose only, which is exactly why buzz-pr-watch and both nekovri entries were
# counted as system-scope by everything that did not read their notes.
# KIND IS LOAD-BEARING FOR THE SAME REASON, one column over (2026-09-03, brief 7). Every
# row here was a timer until the five buzz-agent@* units arrived, so every consumer could
# append ".timer" to a unit name unconditionally and be right 30 times out of 30. Those five
# are Type=simple services with no timer at all — always on, woken by a Buzz mention — and
# an unconditional ".timer" asks the user manager for buzz-agent@marcus.timer, which does
# not exist. systemctl answers "Unit ... could not be found", which renders identically to a
# unit that was deleted. That is the scope defect's exact shape: a live, healthy unit
# reported as missing, in a report whose whole job is to say what is missing.
# So a consumer that lists TIMERS filters `$5=="timer"`, and one that wants unit STATE does
# not need to filter at all (is-active works on both). Neither may append ".timer" blind.
# STATUS FILTER IS THE CONSUMER'S CALL, AND IT MUST BE STATED WHERE IT IS MADE.
#   standing = 28 (22 system + 6 user)   <- what the reporting jobs report on
#   campaign = 3, dormant = 2, spent = 2 <- deliberately excluded from routine reports
# Of the 28 standing, 23 are kind=timer and 5 are kind=service (the buzz-agent@* fleet).
# Do not hardcode those counts anywhere; derive them from this file.
